title: Priya's 5 PR Points: CCL Pass on First Attempt
excerpt: A working mother of two, Priya passed the NAATI CCL test on her first sitting and claimed 5 points for skilled migration. This is exactly how she prepared.
content:
Priya had nine weeks between deciding to migrate and her CCL sitting. She worked full time and had two children under five, so her study time was two hours a night after bedtime.

Her plan: twenty role-play dialogues a week, alternating Nepali-to-English and English-to-Nepali, all recorded and reviewed the next morning on the train. Every Saturday she ran a full mock dialogue with a certified interpreter and fixed the top three errors from the feedback sheet.

Her two biggest early problems were register and names. She kept translating 'G'day' and casual phrasing into formal Nepali, which cost her points on every early mock. Her tutor's fix was a register ladder: a written list of the same sentence in five registers, drilled until she could switch instantly.

By week seven her mock scores sat at 4.2 to 4.5 out of 5. On test day she finished both dialogues with time to spare and scored 4.5 overall.

Five points on her points test lifted her total from 70 to 75 — above the cutoff for her occupation in two consecutive invitation rounds.

The lesson from Priya's story: CCL is a drill sport. Two focused hours a day, weekly scored feedback, and a register drill will take most learners from zero to test-ready inside ten weeks.
